subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes his frustration about the stone and terrain mismatch is legitimate because he prepared reasonably for a different environment.
source_quote: He wasn't wrong about the stone. And his frustration was legitimate — he'd made a reasonable preparation for a reasonable environment, and we'd somehow ended up standing in the one terrain where it didn't apply.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir considered Thorin’s suggestion to fireball the trees but deemed it unworthy of serious thought.
source_quote: I considered this briefly, which is about as much time as it deserves.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz had already decided to get intel out of the situation before announcing his plan to misty step into the tree.
source_quote: I want to get some intel out of this," he said, the way a man says a thing when he's already decided what he's going to do.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir did not rule out the possibility that the tracker might be Jimjar coming to drag them back underground.
source_quote: I did not rule it out.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed Daz’s bird call worked and was pleased it had succeeded.
source_quote: I thought: *good. That actually worked.*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was proud of his own terrible imitation of a bird call.
source_quote: He was very proud of it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum earnestly wondered whether birds are a kind of ooze.
source_quote: Is it a kind of ooze?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum struggled to understand the concept of birds being feathered, as it conflicted with his existing mental framework.
source_quote: I watched the concept try to find somewhere to settle and fail to locate purchase.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes the divine plan has them covered, even if provisionally and subject to revision by evidence.
source_quote: The divine plan has us covered, in the broadest possible sense — or at least I choose to believe it does, provisionally, and correct the belief when the evidence demands it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed movement from the north and interpreted it as a skilled follower, not a random threat.
source_quote: Thorin had picked up something in the terrain earlier — movement from the north, not panicked, not aggressive, careful.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the drow spy was not a predator but a professional doing a job she’d rather not be doing.
source_quote: That combination doesn't say assassin to me. It says someone who got handed a bad assignment and is making the best of it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought the drow spy had been given an assignment that would earn her a sincere complaint if she returned home.
source_quote: Whoever sent a drow to the surface in daylight to shadow a party through open forest had, I thought, given that drow exactly the kind of assignment that earns you a very sincere complaint when you get back home.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was observing the drow spy’s face to read her emotional state, even while she was still stunned.
source_quote: I stood back and let him work, watching the spy's face for what it told me — not yet, she was still too stunned, still in that soft-edged blankness...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the drow spy’s bravery during her approach was a performance masking inner desperation.
source_quote: She'd put on a brave face for the whole approach.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the drow spy was not watching the party but was intensely trying not to look at him.
source_quote: She wasn't watching the party. She was watching me. And working very, very hard to make it look like she wasn't.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized the drow spy’s behavior as a learned social skill from Menzoberranzan — avoiding direct gaze at what one is most interested in.
source_quote: The particular discipline of *not looking at the thing you are most interested in* is one of the first social skills anyone learns in the city.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the drow spy was following him specifically because he was being used as bait to draw out the person who paid for his protection.
source_quote: So basically, you're treating me as bait. You're watching and observing so that when something happens to me, you can go report back what happened to me.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood that House T'sarran’s matron mother was waiting for the person who paid for his protection to reveal themselves on the surface.
source_quote: We are looking for that person, not for you.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recalled a lesson from his training in Menzoberranzan: know who holds the debt before deciding whether to collect it.
source_quote: I thought of something a training instructor had said once... *The first rule of the House: know who holds the debt before you decide whether to collect it.*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt the drow spy’s revelation about being used as bait was a moment of personal revelation, connecting his past to his present danger.
source_quote: The full picture came out under continued pressure... I turned it over once. Twice.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed a fracture in the drow spy’s composure when he offered her a new job.
source_quote: Something shifted in her face. A tiny, involuntary fracture in the composure. *Wait. I might live?*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the prayer beads broke through the drow spy’s professional armor because they represented an unknown, alien threat.
source_quote: Unknown religious ritual from an alien faith, administered by a half-orc? That slipped right past every prepared defense.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum perceived the drow spy as defeated, frustrated, and annoyed after the beads were given and persuasion succeeded.
source_quote: She looked, in the GM's precise summary, defeated, frustrated, annoyed.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed telling the drow spy to report her failure to her matron would be a fate worse than death.
source_quote: He walked up and told her we could simply let her go — report her failure to her matron, "let them know how pathetic you are."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin laughed at the drow spy’s response to his intimidation, but recognized she was still engaging with them.
source_quote: She laughed in his face... She was laughing, but she was also still talking to us...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt no superiority over Thorin’s failed intimidation tactics, recognizing Thorin’s physical honesty as valuable despite his lack of drow political skill.
source_quote: I didn't feel superior about this. Thorin's instincts have saved us too many times for me to feel superior.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz admitted he sounded absurd when he said he’d been underground for a while, realizing how alien it sounded to a drow.
source_quote: I'm drow, but I've been underground for a while.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz corrected himself after realizing his statement sounded absurd, acknowledging he’d been away from home for a while.
source_quote: Let me correct that. I've been away from home for a while.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood that the drow spy’s contemptuous look toward him was rooted in disbelief that he could be so out of touch with drow society.
source_quote: She stared at me... "You realize how absurd that sounds?"

subject: Daz
fact: Daz interpreted the drow spy’s final admission — that she was following him to find the person who paid for his protection — as confirmation of his own significance in a larger, hidden conflict.
source_quote: We are looking for that person, not for you.
